13% of NSCLC carries a homozygous MTAP deletion (MountainTAP-29 trial-in-progress abstract, Peters et al., ESMO Open 2026, 143TiP, doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.106450) x 51% of lung cancers distant at diagnosis (SEER Cancer Stat Facts, lung and bronchus, SEER 21 2016 to 2022) x 81.6% without an alteration that carries a first-line targeted therapy, the complement of the 18.4% in that category among 2023 diagnoses in 8,717 profiled US patients with advanced NSCLC (Wang et al., J Natl Compr Canc Netw 2026, doi 10.6004/jnccn.2025.7131, as the PF-08634404 and rilvegostomig seeds carry it) x 79.3% of stage IV NSCLC without EGFR or ALK starting first-line chemotherapy (2,904 of 3,661, Abernethy et al., PLoS One 2017, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0178420): 0.13 x 0.51 x 0.816 x 0.7932 = 0.042913, about 8,267 patients a year. MountainTAP-29 (NCT07063745) excludes nonsquamous patients with an actionable alteration that has a first-line standard of care, and Abernethy's 79.3% is measured only in patients without EGFR or ALK, so the driver share comes off before it
column12: the driver share is taken at the all-NSCLC rate, which still reads high here: MTAP deletion travels with drivers, and 123 of 258 stage IV MTAP-deleted tumours at MSK (48%) carried an EGFR mutation (Ross et al., J Thorac Oncol 2026;21:103520, PubMed 41260457), an overlap GENIE and C-CAT also find (Ikushima et al., JCO Precis Oncol 2026, PubMed 42172559). The 13% sits between NGS deletion rates of 8.1% to 9.8% in GENIE and 475 of 4,926 (10%) at MSK and MTAP loss by immunohistochemistry in 18.2% (Brune et al., J Thorac Oncol 2026, PubMed 40850616); MountainTAP-29 admits either test. Distant stage at diagnosis leaves out later recurrence, which reads low

column12: the 0.4 multiple is the arguable figure. The case for more: navlimetostat would be the first drug for MTAP-deleted cancer, an oral add-on with a 29% response rate as monotherapy in 35 pretreated NSCLC patients, responses among them in 4 of 7 with EGFR and 2 of 4 with ALK (IASLC release, 8 September 2025), and BMS calls it a potential first-in-class MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor (FY2025 10-K). The case against: it is a third drug on an effective pembrolizumab and chemotherapy backbone, MTAP status needs a sponsor-provided or pre-approved local test before treatment (MountainTAP-29 eligibility), and other MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors, among them Bayer's BAY 3713372 in a first-in-human NSCLC study (same ESMO Open supplement), follow it
